earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only short wordlists (Piron 1996/1997; Chilver & Kaberry 1974; Jeffreys 1962; Schneider 1951); no grammar or phonology of Kwaja exists.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog page for Kwaja [kdz] (language-archives.org, data as of 2025-11-04, read via web.archive.org capture 2026-05-14); also OLAC pages for [nfu] Mfumte and retired [ncp] Ndaktup.
sources.note: Catalog only: for kdz the sole SIL item is McLean 2015 (oai:sil.org:62481); no phonology, orthography guide, lexicon or grammar of Kwaja is archived. ncp: nothing. nfu: Eyoh & Hedinger 2008, McLean 2014, Eyoh & Moveh 2007 alphabet chart.

ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. Change Request 2017-005 (merge [ncp] Ndaktup into [kdz] Kwaja; submitted by G. McLean, SIL).
sources.note: Nothing; its only bibliographic source is McLean 2015.

sources.citation: McLean, Greg L. 2015. A Recorded Text Survey of the Mfumte Speech Varieties and Rapid Appraisal Survey of Dzodinka. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2015-004. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic RTT survey; Kwaja story given only in English translation; sec. 7.4 (p.47) recommends as a future first step for Kwaja to 'collect a 1700-item wordlist, complete a phonology, and write a tentative orthography statement' -- i.e. no Kwaja phonology existed as of 2015.

sources.citation: McLean, Greg L. 2014. A Sketch Grammar of the Central Mfumte Language. Yaounde: SIL Cameroon. 35 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 58664)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; SISTER LANGUAGE (Lus = Central Mfumte, not Kwaja). States only 'Surface tone markings are used and no formal attempt has been made to account for tonal alternation' (sec. 1.5); tone (H/M/L, floating H plural) treated throughout as lexical/grammatical.

sources.citation: Eyoh, Julius A. & Robert Hedinger. 2008. Mfumte orthography guide. Yaounde: NACALCO. (SIL archive 32291)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; SISTER LANGUAGE (Lus dialect of Mfumte). Sec. 3 'Tones' p.8: 'We have identified five surface tones in Mfumte: three level tones: high, mid and low; and two contour tones, rising and falling', with minimal pairs.

sources.citation: Any SIL Cameroon / CABTAL Kwaja' phonology sketch or tentative orthography statement produced after McLean 2015 (recommended there, sec. 7.4); none is in the SIL archive/OLAC as of Nov 2025, but the live sil.org, silcam.org and webonary.org listings for [kdz] could not be checked from our machine (Cloudflare 403).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Would be the first and only first-hand description of Kwaja suprasegmentals; McLean 2015 explicitly called for it and CABTAL supported development of Kwaja as 'Eastern Mfumte'.

sources.citation: Eyoh, Julius A. 2008. Mfumte phonology and revitalisation of the language. D.E.A. dissertation, University of Yaoundé I.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only full phonology in the Mfumteic cluster (Lus/Central Mfumte, sister language of Kwaja); would show whether any stress/accent is described alongside the H/M/L tone system for the group.

sources.citation: Piron, Pascale. 1997. Classification interne du groupe bantoïde, vols. 1-2 (LINCOM Studies in African Linguistics 11-12). München: Lincom Europa.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Largest published body of transcribed Kwaja/Mfumte-group lexical data (tone-marked wordlists); could confirm tonal transcription practice for Kwaja though unlikely to state a stress rule.
